REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: The instructions hand a route-determined election back to the participant, and do it with raw PDF internals. The bullet reads, verbatim: 'Eligibility date (`SingleFelonyCompletionDate`, `MultipleFelonyCompletionDate`, `SingleFelonySatisfiesDate`, or `MulitipleFelonlySatisfiesDate`): add the correct date for the selected statutory route from the sentence/supervision record.' Four defects in one line. (1) The family's OWN field map declares exactly one of those four required before filing — SingleFelonyCompletionDate — and refuses the other three with the reason 'Never a filing fact on this route: single-misdemeanor standard waiting-period route selects SingleFelonyCB, not this'. The delivered instructions therefore contradict the map on three of four items. (2) It asks the participant to determine 'the selected statutory route' when the packet has already selected it by marking SingleFelonyCB on paragraph c, and nowhere in the 6,167-byte file does it say which branch was marked. The completeness contract's own REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING conditions forbid exactly this: 'NOT ROUTE-DETERMINED: an election the route determines may never be required-before-filing. A packet built for one statutory route must state which route it is, rather than asking the participant.' (3) The four names are AcroForm field ids, not captions: none of them is printed anywhere on SCA-C906's face — I extracted all four pages and the printed text runs 'The date of eligibility is: ____' four times with no field name — so a participant cannot find them on the paper. (4) They carry the WVSCA's own artefacts into participant-facing copy: the word 'Felony' on a misdemeanour-only petition, and the misspelling 'MulitipleFelonlySatisfiesDate'. The consequence is not cosmetic. Paragraph c's four branches are four different statutory routes with different clocks, and § 61-11-26(o) makes this relief available once in a lifetime; a participant who dates the wrong branch swears an eligibility basis inconsistent with the box the packet checked. Repair: name the one field the map declares, and say which branch the packet marked. Everything else in the section is sound — I checked all 19 rows the map classifies required_before_filing against the instructions and every one is disclosed, and the map's own reasons cross-reference the instruction bullet by key. ALSO RECORDED, not scored: the packet-set manifest's file entry sets this route's waiting period (one year has run from the later of conviction, release from incarceration and completion of supervision) and the instructions never state it; and SCA-C900, which this family delivers, tells the participant that a served party 'may file a notice of opposition' and that they then have ten days to reply, which the instructions do not mention.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 with A2, and it passes on the first met limb — the packet states the amount, sourced — with the waiver honestly refused and a named checkable authority standing in. I confirmed the figures against the records the route census names, as the task asked. THE $200: the packet says 'The circuit clerk charges the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee, which the official text sets at $200.' The committed track registry's wv_conv_single_misdemeanor destination.detail says 'paying the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee, which the official text sets at $200', the committed route census carries the same sentence on this route key, and the committed packet-set manifest's pay_fee entry says the same. THE $100: 'A person who obtains an order of expungement pays $100 to the records division of the West Virginia State Police under § 61-11-26(n)', which the same three records carry and which the compiled state profile independently corroborates. THE COMPILED PROFILE, checked because the task said the repair deliberately did not draw the number from it: src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/WV-west-virginia.json is named as a requiredSourceId for this route and its only fee sentence is 'For 61-11-26 conviction expungement, the circuit clerk charges the same fee as filing a civil action, and a person who receives an expungement order must pay a $100 West Virginia State Police processing fee.' The string '59-1-11' does not occur in that file at all and $100 is the only dollar figure in it. So the profile is silent on the number rather than in conflict with it, and the $200 comes from two other held records that do state it. THE WAIVER: the packet says 'No held source establishes a waiver route for this filing', explains that the $100 is waived only on a § 61-11-26a petition which is a different route, declines to name a form or to tell the participant they qualify, and names the office to ask — 'the clerk of the circuit court of the county of conviction, the same office you file with'. The manifest's apply_fee_waiver entry says exactly that: 'none under § 61-11-26. The $100 State Police fee is waived only on a § 61-11-26a petition. Any relief from the $200 circuit clerk fee would be under the circuit court's ordinary civil indigency practice, which the controlling review did not establish.' That is the determination's third met branch, done properly and with the authority in the same paragraph as the refusal. CUSTODY NOTE, not a failure: no held BYTES in this container carry § 59-1-11 itself — the $200 lives inside two committed LegalEase-authored records that assert 'the official text sets at $200' and cite source-url https://code.wvlegislature.gov/59-1-11/, which the repository does not hold. Under A2 those committed records ARE the repository, so stating the figure is the correct behaviour; but the figure's freshness rests on a source-acquisition gap rather than on held bytes, and a Captain should know that before promotion. APPLIED A3, WHICH POSTDATES THIS ROW'S BASE AND WHICH I READ FROM THE CAPTAIN HEAD. A3 holds that a record establishes an answer only for the route it actually addresses, and that a line keyed to a different statutory section is a sibling-route inference A2 already forbids. Run on this route's fee fact — the circuit clerk's charge for a § 61-11-26 misdemeanour conviction expungement petition — the test comes out clean, and it shows the repair dodged a live trap of exactly A3's shape. THE RECORDS THAT DO ADDRESS THIS ROUTE: the track registry entry is keyed by trackId to this track, the route census entry is keyed by the full route key, and the packet-set manifest entry is keyed by packetSetId; all three carry the § 59-1-11(a)(1) $200 sentence for this route and nothing else. THE PROFILE, READ PER FACT RATHER THAN PER DOCUMENT: its § 61-11-26 line does address this route's statute, and what it establishes is the $100 State Police fee plus a cross-reference to the civil-action fee with no number — silence on the figure, not a different route's figure. THE TRAP IT AVOIDED: the same compiled profile also carries, three times over, 'For 61-11-25 acquittal/dismissal/diversion/deferred-adjudication expungement, no filing fees or costs are charged' and 'Fee rule: no filing fees or costs are charged for a 61-11-25 action.' Section 61-11-25 is not § 61-11-26. A repairer treating the profile as one held document — which A2 read literally licensed — could have published 'no filing fee' for a petition that in fact costs $200, and the participant would have arrived at the circuit clerk's counter with nothing. That is the California 1203.4 trap with the sign flipped and the stakes higher, and the repair did not walk into it. A3 confirms the sourcing choice the task described was not merely defensible but required.

SERVICE.detail: The packet states the recipients, the method and the timing, sourced, and marks the one recipient the participant must NOT serve. It names the five § 61-11-26(e) recipients in a numbered list — the Superintendent of the West Virginia State Police; the prosecuting attorney of the county of conviction; the chief law-enforcement officer of the arresting agency; the superintendent, warden or Commissioner of Corrections of any institution of confinement; and the circuit, magistrate or municipal court that disposed of the charge — and then states the § 61-11-26(f) carve-out in bold: 'Identified victims are served by the prosecuting attorney, not by you. Do not serve a victim yourself.' It closes with the timing rule, that the page-4 certificate is completed only after service has actually happened. Checked against the records: the track registry destination.detail says 'Serve the five § 61-11-26(e) recipients and file the completed certificate of service. The prosecuting attorney, not the petitioner, serves identified victims'; the route census carries the same; the packet-set manifest's serve_party entry says the same and adds that the prosecuting attorney serves identified victims by first class mail. The manifest also warns that the Utah-style general service-of-process page 'must not be wired to this track; doing so would import a summons, a process server and a 120-day deadline this track does not have', and the packet imports none of that.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet draws its boundary and carries no approval. 'This is a prepared set of official West Virginia forms built for review. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the circuit court will grant expungement.' It names what it will not complete — 'The participant signature, signature date, verification/notary completion, and the entire certificate of service remain blank and protected' — and it refuses to invent the participant's own sworn content, listing grounds for expungement and rehabilitation history as things to 'supply your own truthful' answers for. It also warns off the wrong instrument: 'The included SCA-C900 is an instructions/reference component only; do not complete or file its embedded outdated petition instead of SCA-C906.' Its 'Where these directions come from' section names the exact committed records behind the destination, fee and service claims, which is the honesty this obligation asks for. approval-request.json is REQUESTED with grantedBy null; product-wiring.json carries generationAllowed false, runtimeSelectable false, commercialRoutesOpened 0.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: The strongest fee-and-waiver work of the six families, and it passes A1, A2 and A4 together. It states the answer rather than sending the participant away: "For a true dismissal there is no fee", quoting the manifest; then the $175.00 exception, quoting the manifest; then the switch on the form face, including the NOTE TO CLERK "if this box is checked, do not assess the $175.00 fee"; then the waiver, quoting the manifest's own clause including SNAP, TANF, SSI and representation by a legal services organization, all four of which I confirmed present in participant-instructions.md; then the separate G.S. 15A-150 cost that is expressly not taxed against the petitioner. FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Correct under A1, A2 and A4. The registry states "No fee on the automatic route. County filing fees apply to the fallback petition and vary" and "In forma pauperis relief is available for the fallback petition." The packet does not stop at "ask the clerk": it gives the statewide range of roughly $132 to $215, says expungement petitions typically cost more than limited-access petitions, and warns the participant to treat it as a range to expect rather than their county's figure. I traced that figure to data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/PA.memo.json, which states "The legal review reports a range of roughly $132 to $215 across counties, with expungement petitions generally costing more than limited access petitions. No confirmed statewide schedule exists." SERVICE.finding: The registry's notice rule for the fallback route is "service on the attorney for the Commonwealth concurrently with filing, with 60 days to respond under Rule 790", and the packet carries it with the consequences the registry implies: the petition is served on the Commonwealth, the District Attorney as the attorney for the Commonwealth, which then has 60 days from service to consent, object or do nothing; after that window the judge grants, denies or schedules a hearing; and where it is granted without consent the order is stayed for 30 days while an appeal may be taken. SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Two things fail together and the second is the serious one. First, structurally: the packet has no "when to stop and get help" section at all, on either the guidance page or in participant-instructions.md, and none of the registry's three selfHelpStopConditions is carried as a stop. The participant has not yet obtained a pardon, which the registry says is out of scope and a referral, is nowhere. Whether the pardon is conditional or unconditional cannot be determined from the document is reduced to a description of the difference between the two. The record still appears after the quarterly cycle and the fallback route's availability is unclear is not carried as a stop. Second, and this is a DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A4 violation on the delivered bytes: the guidance page, packet pages 4-5 of both fixtures, tells the participant "This page states no timetable and no criterion for that, because neither is established by the two forms this packet is built from, and an unsourced criterion in a filing instruction is worse than none." The timetable IS established, for this exact route, in three committed records I read at this base. The track registry's packetInstructions for pa_pardon_expungement says "Tell the participant a pardon does not by itself erase the record, and that the Board transmits eligible records to the AOPC quarterly." Its manualCompletionItems carry "Quarterly verification date — Guidance, verification schedule — The participant records when they checked whether the automatic route cleared the record", listed as required before filing. Its packetSet condition on the petition component reads "Generated only where the automatic route has not cleared the record after the quarterly cycle." And src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/PA-pennsylvania.json states "the Board of Pardons transmits eligible records to AOPC quarterly, AOPC sends the record to the court of common pleas, and the court orders expungement after confirming the criteria." The same packet states the quarterly cycle on another page — participant-instructions.md paragraph 4 says the Board transmits eligible records to the AOPC quarterly, in bold. So the packet tells the participant, on the page that goes in the envelope, that it does not state something it states on the page that does not. The guidance page compounds it by narrowing its own source universe to "the two forms this packet is built from", which is precisely the narrowing A2 forbids: the repository's committed records are held sources, not just the PDFs. The registry's named verification schedule is absent from the guidance page in consequence.

postApprovalAuditNotAdjudicated.what: This lane was dispatched to turn a post-approval legal-change audit into a verdict, or to refute it. It could do neither. The three decisive claims -- that the string 223A1 appears nowhere in the family or the rendered fixture while the approved design declares SCCA 223A1 GS (Revised 04/2026) a required component and S.C. Code section 17-22-930 makes the solicitor's blank form mandatory and to the exclusion of all other expungement forms; that the rendered componentSet carries no official_form_reference, records_checklist or fee_instrument_schedule though production-field-map.json declares them; and that eleven of twelve memo tracks route to a prosecutor while the packet is captioned IN THE ......... COURT -- remain exactly as the audit left them. They are not confirmed here and they are not refuted here.
postApprovalAuditNotAdjudicated.consequence: The family's recorded COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN state is neither disturbed nor endorsed by this row. Under the extractor's NON_READING rule a BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM row never enters the current-verdict contest, so vf03's PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT at 9c2b39327f8fe8f9594ee143b1ff11fbcc879c00 stands untouched and unexamined. If the audit is right, a family carrying a proven status is carrying it on a read that predates the audit; that is a reason to grant the re-read quickly, not a reason to write a verdict without one.
postApprovalAuditNotAdjudicated.whyNotWrittenAnyway: A verdict written from the audit's own findings would be this lane laundering someone else's measurement as an independent read. The independence rule and the claim gate exist to stop exactly that. The audit's evidence may well be correct; it is not mine to certify.

REPEATING_ROWS.finding: Row 1 of the DC-33 charge table is filed with a written cell beside two required cells left blank. Canonical writes '2 Charges 1' = 'Possession of a controlled substance' while '1 Counts 1' and '3 Dispositions 1' are refused as classified_unwritable_by_role. A count and a disposition on the participant's own charge table are not court, prosecutor, clerk or notary fields; the role class does not apply to them, and using it is what let the row pass. This is the CR-180 defect the completeness contract exists to catch, arriving through a wrong refusal class. The incompleteRows counter reads 0 because rowKeyOf recognises a row only from an Item/Row/Line token or a label matching 'row N', 'count N' or 'N. ', and this form's names are '1 Counts 1', '2 Charges 1', '3 Dispositions 1', which match none of them, so all three cells key to null and the row is never assembled.

SERVICE.finding: The packet never states who must be served or how. The only two sentences touching service are instructions to the participant to do the work themselves: 'Complete service certificates only after service actually occurs' and 'Confirm current revision, filing destination, local procedures, attachments, service, and proposed-order requirements before filing.' FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: This family IS the fee-and-waiver component, and it is handled to the standard. It does not quote the repealed art. 102.006 $250-$500 range and says in terms where that range came from, so a participant who found it online learns it is from a repealed statute. What it states instead is art. 102.0061 as it now reads: the ordinary county civil ex parte filing fee in district court under (a), and a flat $100 in a justice court or municipal court of record under (b). It opens by telling the participant to check whether they need the form at all, because art. 102.0061(c) and (d) each REQUIRE the fee to be waived in defined circumstances. And it names the larger cost the participant actually controls: art. 55A.254(f) charges $25 per entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, so ten paper-only agencies is $500, twice over, against a fee that art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging for electronic transmission at all. Every figure published is tied to a current statutory subsection.

SERVICE.finding: The packet is explicit that the transmission of the petition and the notice of hearing is the clerk's act and is priced by statute, that art. 55A.254(e) forbids any charge for electronic transmission, and that art. 55A.253(c) requires the clerk to publish the agency e-mail list the participant should use to deduplicate. No certificate of service is generated and none is prefilled.

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Measured by the prescribed instrument, per route and never across. The eight tx_exp_* tracks this family serves record 26 stop conditions between them and the packet's 'When to stop and get help instead' section carries them, including the two hardest: 'you are not a United States citizen' for the registry's immigration condition, and the mixed-outcome multiple-charge stop naming State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P.. On the specific hearing test: no tx_exp_* track records a hearing as the end of self-help — the registry's hearing stops all sit on the tx_nd_* nondisclosure tracks, which this family does not serve and which are not read across — and no sentence in this packet tells the participant to attend a hearing. The section closes by naming who answers what where self-help stops: the district clerk for the fee and the agency list, and it records that the clerk must give the participant this form free and without being asked.

whyTheseAreNotRows.what: These eight refusals are recorded here and NOT appended to the rows array, deliberately.
whyTheseAreNotRows.why: extract-verifier-returns.mjs reads every entry in rows as a verdict ABOUT THE FAMILY and keeps one current verdict per family. Its supersedes() prefers a row whose declared verifiedAtBase is a descendant of the incumbent's. All eight of these families currently carry FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED at bases 7fcfb7d40aafe7bd7350fc735ea09d16524cb757, ebc44031ec7eab29058bfc79a7bc5e1cff089414 and 36d7718a7e48d7f87f18eeaf3b18ed9b3ce545c8; git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms each is an ancestor of this base. A row of mine declaring this base would therefore have superseded all eight.
whyTheseAreNotRows.measuredConsequence: The baseline sweep at this base reports 32 FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED families and names all eight of these among them. Appending these refusals as rows would have taken that list to 24 — eight known-failing families dropped off the repair queue on the strength of a read that never happened, replaced by a verdict that is a statement about this lane rather than about the packet.
whyTheseAreNotRows.therefore: A claim-gate refusal is not a verdict about a family and is not recorded as one. rows is left exactly as the previous lanes wrote it; nothing was superseded, upgraded, downgraded or removed.
whyTheseAreNotRows.aStructuralFindingForCaptain: The extractor has no way to say 'this lane could not look'. Its vocabulary contains BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM and STOPPED, but any row carrying them still competes for the family's single current-verdict slot and still displaces an actionable FAIL. If refused lanes are expected to return rows, the extractor should exclude non-reading verdicts from supersession. Raised, not decided, and not repaired here: this lane may not edit factory scripts.
whyTheseAreNotRows.alsoChecked: All fifteen obligation names already appear in each of these four documents, so adding them here leaves unscoredObligations empty as it already was, and no other lane's PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT row changes its downgrade state.
